topics.label: Introduction to cancer hallmarks and lecture overview
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer introduces the learning outcomes, historical framework, and core concept of the hallmarks of cancer.

topics.label: Deregulation of growth signaling pathways
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how mutations in receptor tyrosine kinase and Wnt/beta-catenin pathways enable growth signal autonomy and insensitivity to growth inhibitory signals.

topics.label: Differentiation block in tumor development
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how cancer cells fail to undergo terminal differentiation, using examples from hematopoietic malignancies and intestinal epithelium.

topics.label: Evasion of apoptosis
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic details how mutations in p53 and Bcl-2 family regulators disrupt the mitochondrial pathway to prevent programmed cell death.

topics.label: Replicative immortality, senescence, and telomere maintenance
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine the limits of cellular replication, telomere biology, senescence triggers via p53 stress responses, and cancer mechanisms to reactivate telomerase.

topics.label: Altered cancer metabolism and the Warburg effect
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe metabolic rewiring in cancer cells, including aerobic glycolysis, tissue-specific metabolic profiles, and oncometabolites generated by Krebs cycle mutations.

topics.label: Tumor angiogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic addresses the angiogenic switch and the mechanisms by which tumors induce new blood vessel growth to sustain nutrient and oxygen supply.

topics.label: Mechanisms, barriers, and genetics of tumor metastasis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics analyse the multistep metastatic cascade, the seed-and-soil hypothesis, liquid biopsies of circulating tumor cells, and the genomic features of metastatic clones.

topics.label: Concluding remarks and summary
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer summarizes the overarching themes of the cancer hallmarks and concludes the lecture.
